summary.summary: PARTIAL, and it decides the unit's question: with rates depending only on the contents and occupancies within distance one of the two sites of the event, modulo the symmetries fixing the event, stationarity of pi under inertial streaming is FEASIBLE on the three-record sector of the 3x3x3 window at (p,q,r) = (3,1,2) - at c = 1 with 332 equations over 274 patterns and at the neutral scale c_0 = 1/2 with 334 equations, in both cases with strictly positive rates and every equation verified in exact rational arithmetic (the particular rate interval depends on which LP vertex is returned and is printed by the run, not fixed here) - but it becomes INFEASIBLE as soon as a single four-record configuration is adjoined, namely (1,0,1):-x, (1,0,2):+z, (1,1,2):-x, (1,2,1):-x, for which an exact Farkas certificate y satisfies (A^T y)_j <= 0 at all 275 patterns with sum -36/5 < 0; the machinery is validated against block 50's own figures (70200 configurations, the local clock defective in 3168 of them, largest defect 3 at the block's stated witness), and record number and the multiset of contents are conserved by every event for any rates at all

review: No prior attempt. I validated the machinery against block 50's own published figures first - 70200 configurations, the local clock defective in exactly 3168 of them, largest defect 3 at the block's stated witness - and only then computed anything new. The three-record feasibility problem is FEASIBLE with strictly positive local rates at both c = 1 and the neutral scale, with an LP proposing and exact Fraction arithmetic verifying every one of the 332 and 334 equations. But adjoining a SINGLE four-record configuration, (1,0,1):-x (1,0,2):+z (1,1,2):-x (1,2,1):-x, makes it infeasible, and I give an exact Farkas certificate: a rational y with (A^T y)_j <= 0 at all 275 patterns and sum -36/5 < 0. So the answer decides YES at three records and the YES does not generalize; the local clock's three-record defect is repairable and the real obstruction is one record higher. Number and the content multiset are conserved by every event for any rates at all, so the whole question is stationarity. Two limits I want on the record: the infeasibility is for THIS locality class only and I did NOT do the part (c) enlargement with a momentum-conserving null event, so no local rule of any kind is ruled out; and everything is one 3x3x3 window at (3,1,2). I also caught myself quoting LP rate intervals in the summary that change between runs because the vertex changes, and removed them.
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 2 of 4: Is there a LOCAL rule under which inertial streaming keeps the rule's law stationary?. SETTING (block 50; open PR titled 'ail50: inertia joined with the rule's pair weights by a clock'): six-axis menu on a periodic cubic window; a configuration is a set of occupied sites with one of six contents each (contents 0..5 = +x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z); the law with vacancies gives it the weight pi(C) = product over adjacent occupied pairs of c omega(a, b), omega = p for equal contents, q for opposite, r for orthogonal ((p, q, r) = (3, 1, 2) is the campaign's reference, c = 1 or the neutral scale c_0 = 6/(p + q + 4r)). Inertial streaming (block 44): the record at x with content s has the target x + e_s; an empty target is entered; an occupied target exchanges contents with the record. ESTABLISHED: every record has exactly one event and exactly one predecessor (the same record one site back if the site behind is empty, the two contents exchanged back if it is occupied), so with every event of C at the rate 1/pi(C) (GLOBAL clock) pi is stationary for any weights and density; with the event of the record at x at the rate 1/pi_x(C) (LOCAL clock; pi_x = product of the pair weights of site x) the balance defect is out - in = sum over records whose site behind b is occupied (content u) of W_0 [A_b(u) - A_x(u)], zero for two records and non-zero at three (3168 of the 70200 three-record configurations with a record at the origin on the 3x3x3 torus; largest 3 at (0,0,0):+y, (0,0,1):+z, (0,1,0):+y). Exact code: the block's runner scripts/admissibility_rule_inertia_joined_with_the_rules_pair_weights_by_a_clock_*.py and specs/supervisor_control_block50_refuter.py on the PR branch. TASK: decide it on the three-record sector, then say what generalizes. (a) Set up the linear feasibility problem: unknown non-negative rates for every event (a move into an empty target; an exchange of contents with an occupied target), where a rate may depend only on the contents and occupancies of the sites within distance one of the two sites of the event, modulo the lattice symmetries that fix the event (covariance). Constraints: for every three-record configuration of the 3x3x3 torus, the flow of pi in equals the flow out; moves must have positive rates. Solve it exactly (rational arithmetic; an LP solver may propose, exact arithmetic must verify) for (p, q, r) = (3, 1, 2) at c = 1 and at c_0 = 1/2. (b) If feasible: exhibit the rule in closed form if you can, check it at four records on a sample, and say whether number and momentum are still conserved event by event. (c) If infeasible: give a certificate (a dual vector), and then enlarge the family: allow an additional momentum-conserving event when the target is occupied (for instance both records keep their contents and nothing happens, or the pair re-draws its contents on its momentum class), and repeat. (d) State the result as a theorem with its scope. check.py: exact verification of the balance at every three-record configuration for the rule or the certificate you give.  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/local-clock-for-inertia-with-weights/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route.
